record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: What are the explicit correction terms, beyond the leading linear-in-temperature contribution, to the low-temperature specific heat of the side-coupled quantum-dot model in an interacting Luttinger-liquid environment, and do their exponents indeed match the exponents inferred earlier from the renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation?

evidence.quote: The corrections are still to be calculated but the exponents are expected to agree with those found earlier.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a side-coupled quantum-dot model in which a single interacting electronic level (the dot) is tunnel-coupled to a one-dimensional interacting Luttinger-liquid lead characterized by Luttinger parameter K (with K<1 for repulsive interactions). The dot has on-site energy ε_d and is coupled to the lead at a single point by a tunneling amplitude t, with the lead described by the standard bosonized Luttinger Hamiltonian.

A renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation n_d(T) at low temperature predicts a leading low-temperature behaviour together with subleading corrections governed by anomalous interaction-dependent exponents α_i(K).

Determine the explicit low-temperature expansion of the impurity specific heat C_imp(T) of this model beyond the leading linear-in-T contribution, in the form
   C_imp(T) = γ T + Σ_i a_i(K) T^{β_i(K)} + …,
giving the coefficients a_i(K) and the exponents β_i(K). In particular, decide whether the exponents β_i(K) coincide with the exponents α_i(K) extracted from the renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation.
artifact.category_tag: quantum impurity models in Luttinger liquids
artifact.status_search_result: No published computation of the explicit subleading corrections to the impurity specific heat of the side-coupled quantum-dot in a Luttinger-liquid environment was located. Existing works on quantum dots coupled to Luttinger-liquid leads (e.g., the Bethe-ansatz/edge studies and underscreened-Kondo-in-Luttinger results) discuss exponents from the dot occupation/capacitance and Fermi-liquid-like leading specific heat, but the matching of subleading specific-heat exponents to those derived from the RG analysis of the dot occupation appears to remain to be carried out.

status_evidence.title: Quantum dot at a Luttinger liquid edge
status_evidence.snippet: Exact solution of a quantum dot coupled to a Luttinger liquid edge; identifies critical exponents at weak and strong coupling.
status_evidence.claim: Related exact-solution work treats exponents but does not give explicit subleading specific-heat corrections matched to RG-derived dot-occupation exponents.

status_evidence.title: Underscreened Kondo impurities in a Luttinger liquid
status_evidence.snippet: Leading specific heat is Fermi-liquid-like with anomalous power-law subleading terms.
status_evidence.claim: Anomalous subleading specific-heat exponents are anticipated in similar Luttinger-impurity setups, but the side-coupled dot computation/comparison is not provided.

status_evidence.title: Charging of a quantum dot coupled to Luttinger-liquid leads
status_evidence.snippet: Studies dot occupation/charging exponents via RG.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the dot-occupation exponents but does not explicitly compute matching specific-heat corrections.
